This is a late response but…

The entire point of the article is that this looming threat of cosmic proportions is completely mundane. This star feels nothing. It knows nothing. It is no more sentient than a rock.

This is just a normal, boring pulsar (well, as boring as a pulsar can be). Despite the world of terrors, cosmic and terrestrial, we are still trapped in a universe which just doesn't care, anomalous or not.

I didn't want it to be some encroaching threat trying to kill us because that would have taken away from the intended point big time.

Thanks for the read :)

item.content:encoded:
I'm tempted, but I'll have to give this a no-vote for now.

Quick crit
Quick crit

The article could use a few more passes for grammar and tone,

"were just a fluke-one of cosmic proportions." Needs a comma, or semicolon.

"Upon the completion and population of Foundation Lunar Area-32, my team has performed more detailed measurements of SCP-1548." 'Upon' is too passive for the proceeding 'performed'. 'Shortly after' and 'my team was able to', or 'Following the' and 'my team found the time', etc.

"primary research into how SCP-1548 operates and possible methods of termination are to be relocated there." Doesn't feel appropriate, really. It's a celestial object several million times larger than Earth. While it's very reminiscent of the original article, "planetary evacuation" might be a more realistic response than trying to "terminate" a star.

"Researcher Natalie came to me with these concerns and made the proposal to reclassify SCP-1548 as -EX herself. I've made the decision to accept her proposal." Then why is the article listed as "Item #: SCP-1548" instead of "Item #: SCP-1548-EX"? Oddly, the only implication that the article is under revision is the " Euclid Keter" section, which itself is outdated. Also, an 05 giving a single researcher a shout-out seems out of place, and this entire line guts the finality of the "god has a strange sense of humor" line before it.

Overall, the article is either rushed, or derivative. For the former, If this is intended to stand apart from the "Hateful Star", than a lot more elements need to be fleshed out so it feels like a complete article. For the latter, if this is intended to be a substitute or off-shoot of the "Hateful Star", than I'd like to see more deviation beyond the lunar base, and the twist ending.

The twist itself is really why I've landed on no-vote. Simply making the "Hateful Star" an -EX, and it's pulses a fluke of nature / human perception just doesn't hit me that hard. I like SCPs with the "science just hasn't caught up yet" twist, but not so much in this case.

I think the fact that the star is pre-established to be "incredibly unstable" and have an "unpredictable axis" makes it lack the perceived maliciousness of the original article. Without it, it's just a random stellar object that seems to be giving off aggressive messages. If it can create radiation bursts strong enough to devastate our planetary ecology… why doesn't it just do that? Does it not know where we are? The intent, the threat, just isn't there.
